D01.automated: Exact editor bytes, header-only changes, binary retention, Content-Length, compressed bodies, and body-only HTTP/2/gRPC framing.
D01.live: An unchanged intercepted GET reached the fixture with CRLF headers and an empty body. Repeater also sent an unchanged GET successfully.

D02.automated: Preloaded flow navigation, flags, detail, filters, exports, new-flow delivery, and export errors.
D02.live: Five saved rows appeared before new traffic. With one visible filtered row, session JSON and HAR each retained all five flows.

D03.automated: Asynchronous resend, immutable snapshots, cancellation, bounded progress, duplicate prevention, and shutdown.
D03.live: Help remained responsive during a held response. Global cancellation stopped the active request.

D04.automated: Incoming/outgoing WebSocket scope and toggle combinations, forward/edit/drop, and continued connection use.
D04.live: Response interception held an incoming echo. The client received the edited payload.

D05.automated: Exactly-once injection capture, direction/opcode/bytes, partial-write errors, optional metadata, and export round trips.
D05.live: Saved history retained one injected outbound frame, a separate ordinary echo, and one injected inbound frame. A closed-session send retained its draft.

D06.automated: Reflow after terminal and split resize, including bottom anchoring.
D06.live: Open detail remained at 100% with ENDTOKEN visible after shrinking to 80x24 and growing again.

D07.automated: Cell-bounded detail, Repeater, prompts, status, compact panes, and tiny terminals.
D07.live: Exercised 160x48, 120x36, 80x24, tiny terminals, extreme splits, and all four built-in themes.

D08.automated: HTTP code/reason separate from lifecycle, existing errors, single direction labels, and injection markers.
D08.live: HTTP 500 traffic and WebSocket injection history displayed distinct status and provenance.

D09.automated: Effective custom and unbound modal controls and canonical default hints.
D09.live: A Ctrl+G CLI override superseded Ctrl+A in the configuration. Help displayed the rebound H action and Ctrl+G footer.

D10.automated: Global actions across modal owners, suspended drafts/cursors, pending and unknown leaders, collision rejection, and mouse ownership.
D10.live: Pane/help round trips preserved editor and Repeater state. Global commands remained available during pause inspection and jobs.

U01.automated: Held-flow, direction, token identity, queue count, and selected-row distinction.
U01.live: The none theme displayed one held request and one queued request while a different traffic row remained selected.

U02.automated: Pause arrival preserved terminal, filter, command, and editor input; FIFO token-specific resolution.
U02.live: A held request did not steal terminal focus. Terminal input continued before reversible pause inspection.

U03.automated: Status/size/protocol columns, long targets, payload access, sorting, and rendered mouse row mapping.
U03.live: Sorted and flagged loaded traffic, attack results, and narrow views retained comparison columns.

U04.automated: Attack count rules and overflow, actual outcomes, stale-session isolation, cancellation races, and joined shutdown.
U04.live: All five modes produced 1/5/2/2/6 requests. Closing Repeater retained global progress and cancellation.

U05.automated: Distinct empty capture, filter, and flagged-only states with configured hints.
U05.live: Captured no-traffic, zero-filter-match, and zero-flagged-row views.

U06.automated: Raw/expanded representations, safe controls, preview caps, adaptive hex, scrolling, and unchanged stored/export bytes.
U06.live: Toggled raw/expanded detail and retained the final long-body content after resize.

L01.automated: NUL recognition, aliases, explicit overrides, one-byte passthrough, CLI/file precedence, and every-context collision checks.
L01.live: NUL leader commands worked throughout the TUI. Ordinary Ctrl+A reached readline. An explicit Ctrl+A leader required a double press to send one literal byte.

cleanup: The supervised fixture and terminal-driver processes were stopped. Temporary fixture scripts, captures, and binaries were removed.
scope_note: All live traffic used isolated local fixtures. Transparent Linux interception and external production services were not exercised.
